title: Storage pricing: S3 classes, EBS and EFS

kcs.statement: S3 cost has four parts: gigabyte-months stored (priced by storage class), requests, data retrieval for infrequent-access and Glacier classes, and data transferred out.

Infrequent-access and Glacier classes cost less to store but charge per-GB retrieval fees and have minimum storage durations: 30 days for Standard-IA, 90 days for Glacier Flexible Retrieval and 180 days for Glacier Deep Archive.
EBS bills for the gigabytes you provision whether or not you fill them, while EFS and S3 bill only for the gigabytes actually stored.

problem_ideas: A 500 GB EBS volume holds 50 GB of data: predict how many GB are billed, and compare with the same data on EFS.
An object moved to Glacier Deep Archive is deleted after 60 days: predict how many days of storage are charged.
Logs are read daily for a week, then almost never: which S3 classes over time and why?
A team moved hot images to Standard-IA and its bill went up: explain the retrieval-fee trap.
List the four line items an S3 bill can contain for a public download bucket.
A backup archive must be kept 7 years and is restored perhaps once: choose the class and name the cost trade-off.
